Welcome
Welcome to the Glebe School website. It is a great honour and privilege to be the Headteacher of a such a remarkable school. Situated in West Wickham, we are a large special education needs school which caters to pupils with a range of learning needs. Our reputation is far reaching, where we are celebrated for being an aspirational and pupil centred school. This is underpinned through an excellent curriculum offer as well as wider support and interventions that help develop the full potential of all our pupils. At Glebe, we believe that this approach is fundamental for a child’s success, as the development of character sits firmly alongside academic achievement for life-long success.
It is our vision to ensure that we prepare all of our pupils to live life independently, responsibly and successfully and this is reflected through our curriculum offer. Subjects such as Sport, Music, Drama, Art and Food Technology sit alongside the core subjects of English, Maths and Science. This is supported with a variety of extracurricular activities, clubs and therapeutic support. As a result of this, our pupils enjoy being at Glebe and consequently make exceptional progress from their starting points.
Please take time to browse through our website where you will learn more about our values, policies and approaches.
We hope you find it informative.
Ian Travis

Leading Parent Partnership Award
We are delighted to be be LPPA accredited 2025-2028
At Glebe, we are committed to working closely with parents, carers, and our local community to support children’s learning and wellbeing. Research shows that when parents are engaged, children’s achievement, behaviour, and attendance improve.
As you will know from our newsletters and emails, The Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA) recognises schools that build strong, effective partnerships with parents and carers. It helps schools identify areas for improvement and ensures that parents feel welcomed, informed, and involved in their children’s learning. The Award is a key tool for school self-evaluation, complements the standards required by Ofsted, Investors in People and other national awards as well as providing ongoing evidence relevant to the school Self Evaluation Form (SEF).
Show commitment to achieving the LPPA
Implement effective plans to maintain LPPA standards
Create a welcoming, communicative, and friendly environment for parents
Promote parent participation in children’s learning and provide joint parent–child activities
Provide a supportive induction for new parents
Offer relevant, accessible guidance to help parents support learning
Produce parent-friendly policies to strengthen home–school links and improve attendance, progress, and participation
Support parents through transitions as children move through or leave the school
Review achievements against LPPA objectives and plan for the future.
Read all letters and publicity we send home
Come along to our events if you can
Complete any questionnaires we send you as honestly as you can

Challenge Partners
Challenge Partners is a collaborative network of over 350 schools nationally. It is a practitioner-led charity that enables collaboration between schools to enhance the life chances of all children. Schools in this network of excellence take part in annual quality assurance reviews in which they are supported and challenged to find collaborative solutions.
The school is visited by a team of external reviewers from Challenge Partners to carry out a collaborative peer to peer review of our school.
In our most recent inspection (November 2024), after two rigorous days of observing teaching across the school, analysis of school planning/evaluation and meetings with school leaders, we are absolutely delighted to report that Glebe is once again considered a ‘Leading’ school.

Safeguarding and Our Curriculum
At Glebe, safeguarding is embedded within our curriculum and culture, not only in lessons, but within our wider curriculum, daily routines, language and conversations. Our pupils, are taught how to stay safe, how to protect themselves from harm and how to take responsibility for their safety at school and within the community. Through this, we ensure a caring, safe, secure and inclusive environment, so that pupils are happy, confident, achieve their best, make a successful transition into adulthood and lead fulfilling lives.
Our broad and balanced curriculum gives pupils the opportunity to acquire the knowledge, understanding and skills that significantly impacts personal development, behaviour and welfare; physical and mental well-being, to support safeguarding themselves. We encourage pupils to ask questions, share their concerns and reflect on their thoughts.
There are many opportunities throughout our learning in our curriculum to explore safeguarding issues, for example through Tutor Time, Assemblies, Pastoral Team conversations and in lessons. We are mindful of the needs of our pupils therefore are considerate in the delivery of all information. Topics we cover include:
